claims.text: A cache stores a response and reuses it to answer a later equivalent request without forwarding that request to the origin server.
claims.source_hint: RFC 9111 §1 Introduction and §1.1 definitions of cache and cache entry

claims.text: Caches are not only on the server side: a private cache belongs to one client (a browser), a shared cache serves more than one user (a proxy), and both follow the same response instructions; only a copy in the client's own cache saves the network trip too.
claims.source_hint: RFC 9111 §1.1 (private cache vs shared cache), §3 Storing Responses in Caches

claims.text: GET is the method whose responses caches normally store; storing the response to an unsafe method such as POST or DELETE is not the ordinary case.
claims.source_hint: RFC 9111 §3 Storing Responses in Caches (conditions on the request method), §4 Constructing Responses from Caches

claims.text: The Cache-Control response directive max-age gives the freshness lifetime in seconds: a stored response is stale once its age (time since the origin generated or last successfully validated it) exceeds that number, and it may be reused without revalidation until then.
claims.source_hint: RFC 9111 §4.2 Freshness, §4.2.1 Calculating Freshness Lifetime, §5.2.2.1 max-age response directive

claims.text: A stored response past its freshness lifetime is stale; stale does not mean discarded — the cache keeps it and normally revalidates it with the origin before reusing it, unless serving it stale is explicitly permitted or the cache is disconnected.
claims.source_hint: RFC 9111 §4.2 Freshness, §4.2.4 Serving Stale Responses, §4.3 Validation

claims.text: ETag is a response header field carrying a validator for the current version of the representation.
claims.source_hint: RFC 9110 §8.8.3 ETag; §8.8.1 Validator Fields

claims.text: A client revalidates by repeating the request with an If-None-Match header carrying the stored ETag; the origin compares it against the current version.
claims.source_hint: RFC 9110 §13.1.2 If-None-Match; RFC 9111 §4.3.1 Sending a Validation Request

claims.text: When the validator still matches, the origin answers 304 Not Modified with no body and the cache reuses the stored response to answer its own client with 200; when it does not match, the origin answers 200 with the new representation.
claims.source_hint: RFC 9110 §15.4.5 304 Not Modified; RFC 9111 §4.3.3 Handling a Validation Response

claims.text: 304 is not an error: it is a 3xx answer that sends the client to the copy it already holds, as if that copy were the content of a 200, which is why the origin deliberately sends no body.
claims.source_hint: RFC 9110 §15.1 status class list, §15.4 Redirection 3xx, §15.4.5 304 Not Modified

claims.text: A response with no Cache-Control field is not thereby uncacheable: a cache may still store and reuse it using its own heuristics for how long it stays fresh.
claims.source_hint: RFC 9111 §4.2.2 Calculating Heuristic Freshness

claims.text: In the Caddyfile at tag stage-0, the handle /cached.html block scopes the directives inside it to that path, where header sets Cache-Control: max-age=60; no other route in the file sets Cache-Control (other routes do use header, for Content-Type, Location and Set-Cookie).
claims.source_hint: Caddy 2 docs, Caddyfile directives: header and handle; plus examples/don-hang Caddyfile at tag stage-0, lines 34-74

claims.text: Serving /cached.html with file_server produces a response carrying an Etag header. Caddy's documentation does not state how the value is computed, so the lesson names no mechanism and says only that the line is masked, as outputs/unstable.regex requires of values that can differ between runs.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang outputs/stage-0/scripts/http/cache-headers.txt step 1; Caddy 2 docs file_server pages, which carry no ETag text

claims.text: Running scripts/http/cache-headers.sh at tag stage-0 prints 200 with Cache-Control: max-age=60 and an Etag for /cached.html, 304 for the request quoting that Etag, and reports that /index.html carries no Cache-Control header.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang outputs/stage-0/scripts/http/cache-headers.txt (captured by CI)

claims.text: The Etag value in the captured output is shown as ... because outputs/unstable.regex masks values that change between runs before the captured file is compared.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang scripts/capture-output.sh and outputs/unstable.regex at tag stage-0

claims.text: Step 2 of the script fetches the current Etag immediately before sending it back in If-None-Match, so it can never be quoting an outdated validator; a client that stored a response earlier can be.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang scripts/http/cache-headers.sh lines 13-16 at tag stage-0

claims.text: Reusing a stored response trades a saved round trip against the risk that the origin changed the representation inside the freshness lifetime, and nobody behind the cache can tell that it did.
claims.source_hint: RFC 9111 §1 Introduction (caches improve performance at the cost of possible staleness), §4.2 Freshness

claims.text: A request for a page you have already visited is an ordinary request, so a stored response that is still fresh can answer it without the origin being contacted at all — including copies held by proxies you never control.
claims.source_hint: RFC 9111 §4 Constructing Responses from Caches, §4.2 Freshness

claims.text: Each step of the script is a separate command that keeps nothing from the one before, so there is no stored copy for max-age=60 to govern: the captured run shows step 2 reaching the origin and being answered 304 seconds after step 1, so a revalidation may be made at any moment.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang scripts/http/cache-headers.sh and outputs/stage-0/scripts/http/cache-headers.txt at tag stage-0

claims.text: A request may itself forbid reuse of a stored response: the no-cache request directive tells caches not to satisfy the request without successful validation on the origin, which is what a deliberate refresh can send; freshness alone cannot force a user agent to reload.
claims.source_hint: RFC 9111 §5.2.1.4 no-cache request directive; §4.2 Freshness (last paragraph, on forcing a reload)

claims.text: scripts/up.sh starts the lab (static site, database and lab box); the first line of cache-headers.sh re-executes the script inside the lab box via scripts/lab-run.sh, so the reader runs only the lesson script and installs nothing else.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang scripts/up.sh, scripts/lab-run.sh, scripts/http/cache-headers.sh lines 4-5 at tag stage-0

claims.text: The curl invocations in the script are given different options, and the captured run shows the consequence: step 1 prints header lines, step 2 prints only a status code.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang scripts/http/cache-headers.sh and outputs/stage-0/scripts/http/cache-headers.txt at tag stage-0
